Operator context describes id and airport_ref as the publisher's internal integer identifiers, and their sample_values are consistently plain digit strings with no leading zeros, so both are cast from VARCHAR to INTEGER.

surface has distinct_count 239 with values like ASP-G, ASPH-CONC-F, and operator context states the surface codes are not a fixed list, so it is kept as a free-text string renamed surface_code rather than constrained to an enum.

le_displaced_threshold_ft and he_displaced_threshold_ft have null_rate 0.884201 and 0.899907 respectively, well above 0.5, so both are retained as nullable sparse measures rather than dropped, per rule 7.

The le_ and he_ latitude/longitude/elevation/heading columns each carry null_rate between roughly 0.22 and 0.28, reflecting runway ends whose geometry was never captured; all are retained nullable rather than imputed or dropped.

purpose: This table holds one row per runway end-pair record from OurAirports, giving each runway's identifiers, physical dimensions, surface, lighting and closure status, and the geographic and heading details of its low-numbered and high-numbered ends, feeding airport infrastructure and flight-planning analyses that join back to the airports table via airport_reference_id or airport_identifier.
usage: Join to the silver airports table on airport_identifier (matching that table's ident) or airport_reference_id (matching its internal key); treat runway_id as the unique grain and filter on is_closed when only operational runways are wanted. Many measure and position columns (length_feet, width_feet, the low_end_/high_end_ latitude, longitude, elevation, heading, and displaced_threshold_feet columns) are nullable and must be null-checked before aggregation, especially the displaced_threshold_feet columns which are populated on fewer than 12% of rows.
limitations: No deduplication was needed since duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, but roughly 22-28% of rows lack low-end or high-end latitude, longitude, elevation, and heading values, and over 88% lack displaced_threshold_feet on either end, so geometric and threshold analyses will only cover a minority of runway ends; surface_code remains an open, unvalidated vocabulary rather than a constrained enum.
